stemBlocks.value: The cash price of a refrigerator is $80 000. It can be bought on hire purchase by paying a deposit of $10 000 and 12 monthly instalments of $7 000. (a) Calculate the hire purchase price. (Only part (a) appears in this extract.)
Think first: The hire purchase price is everything the buyer hands over: the deposit plus every instalment.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p020-q21 from workbook page 20.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the total paid in instalments.
Compare with the cash price to see the cost of credit.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply the monthly instalment by the number of months, then add the deposit.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) The hire purchase price is $94 000, which is $14 000 more than the cash price.

whyThisWorks.value: Hire purchase spreads payment over time and the seller charges for that convenience, so the total paid always exceeds the cash price. The deposit is part of the purchase, not a separate fee, which is why it is added rather than ignored.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding the deposit to the cash price instead of to the instalment total.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding the deposit to the cash price instead of to the instalment total.
Avoid this: Forgetting the deposit and giving $84 000.
Avoid this: Dividing rather than multiplying by 12.

examTip.value: Set hire purchase working out as a short list: deposit, instalments, total. Later parts then read straight off your list.
